text: Both clients: a resolved currency save persists the email-derived initials default as an explicit override

Fixed in f6564c3. Both clients now omit the initials key entirely from the
currency-only save, rather than the ticket's suggested "send it only when it
differs from the derived default" — currency and initials are separate forms on
both clients, so the currency save has no business writing initials at all, and
the server already treats an absent key as leave-unchanged (T-87). That also
stops a genuine override being needlessly re-stamped on an unrelated save.

No server change needed: absent-key semantics already do the right thing, so
exposing whether initials is a stored override vs derived (the other fix idea in
this ticket) would be a wire change with no remaining caller.

Two existing tests asserted the OLD behavior and were inverted. The web test that
checked this conditionally (`if ("initials" in body)`) — flagged as a Minor in
the T-99..T-102 whole-branch review because it could never actually skip — is now
unconditional. Added one regression test per client pinning the reported case:
preload resolves to the derived default, currency save must not send it.

Note the initials form itself still sends whatever is displayed, which for an
account with no override is the derived default. That is a deliberate user action
on that field, so it's left as-is — saving the initials form pins the initials,
which is what it looks like it does.

verify-all green (server 257 / web 121 / android 271 + lint). NOT released —
user asked to hold this for the next batch.
